title: Persia had no navy. So how did it take Hormuz back?

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Persia had no navy. So how did it take Hormuz back?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: It borrowed one. In 1622, Shah Abbas made a deal with the English East India Company.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: English ships bombarded the fortress, while Persian troops closed in around it.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Hmm. How long did it hold out?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: About ten weeks. Then the Portuguese surrendered.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: And what did the English get out of it?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: A promise of half the customs. And the trade moved to the mainland, to a port named after the shah: Bandar Abbas.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Meanwhile, Hormuz island slowly emptied.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Okay, so why does the strait matter again?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Oil. In 1908, British prospectors struck oil in Persia. Soon tankers filled the Gulf.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: And then came the tanker war, right?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Exactly. Iran and Iraq were at war. By the end of 1987, Iraq had attacked two hundred and eighty-three ships, and Iran one hundred and sixty-eight.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: So in 1987, the US Navy began escorting Kuwaiti tankers under the American flag.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: In April 1988, an American frigate hit a mine.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: And the navy struck back in a single day of battle.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Then, that July, an American cruiser shot down an Iranian airliner. The US said it had mistaken it for a fighter jet. All 290 people on board died.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: That's terrible. How did it all end?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: A few weeks later, Iran and Iraq agreed to a ceasefire.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: And today?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Today, about twenty million barrels a day still squeeze through the same narrow gap. So whoever threatens it can still shake the world.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: If you enjoyed this, give it a like and follow History Sketches for more.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: And tell us in the comments: what do you think, and what should we explore next?
Thanks for watching!
